title: The Blubber Glove: Parent Guide
endLine: Blubber makes no heat. It slows warmth from leaving the body.

scenes.tts: Picture a seal swimming in icy water all day with only short hair. How does it stay warm? With four zip bags and vegetable shortening, your child can feel the answer at your kitchen table.
scenes.caption: Picture a seal swimming in icy water all day with only short hair. How does it stay warm? With four zip bags and vegetable shortening, your child can feel the answer at your kitchen table.
scenes.visual: Friendly schematic drawing filling most of the frame: a stylized seal glides slowly through icy blue water with gently bobbing ice chunks. A clean cutaway on the seal's side glows softly, then morphs smoothly into two clear plastic-bag mittens beside a bowl of ice water on a warm kitchen tabletop.
scenes.narration: Picture a seal swimming in icy water all day with only short hair. How does it stay warm? With four zip bags and vegetable shortening, your child can feel the answer at your kitchen table.

scenes.visual: Carried kitchen-tabletop schematic stays softly animated with bobbing ice cubes while bold, high-contrast title text 'The Blubber Glove' settles cleanly across the upper frame.

scenes.tts: In this thirty-minute activity, your child practices making a guess and checking it right away. They compare how their hands feel and check whether the result repeats after switching mittens. Stay with your child from setup through cleanup.
scenes.caption: In this thirty-minute activity, your child practices making a guess and checking it right away. They compare how their hands feel and check whether the result repeats after switching mittens. Stay with your child from setup through cleanup.
scenes.visual: On the carried kitchen tabletop, a simple schematic checklist icon animates softly in three gentle beats: a speech-bubble guess mark, two mittens side by side with one highlighted layer, and a curved swap arrow. Keep at most five clean elements on screen, large high-contrast labels.
scenes.narration: In this thirty-minute activity, your child practices making a guess and checking it right away. They compare how their hands feel and check whether the result repeats after switching mittens. Stay with your child from setup through cleanup.

scenes.tts: Set out four matching gallon-size zip bags, tape, towels, a timer, and a bowl. Check the vegetable shortening label for food allergies. Put about two cups in one bag. Slip a second bag inside. Tape the folded rims together and leave the inner bag open. Spread the shortening about a finger's width around the inner bag.
scenes.caption: Set out four matching gallon-size zip bags, tape, towels, a timer, and a bowl. Check the vegetable shortening label for food allergies. Put about two cups in one bag. Slip a second bag inside. Tape the folded rims together and leave the inner bag open. Spread the shortening about a finger's width around the inner bag.
scenes.visual: Schematic tabletop view: four zip bags, a shortening tub, tape roll, towels, timer, and large bowl appear cleanly. Two bags step forward into cross-section: pale cream shortening scoops into the outer bag, the inner bag slides inside, tape seals the folded rim open, and the shortening spreads evenly about a finger's width thick.
scenes.narration: Set out four matching gallon-size zip bags, tape, towels, a timer, and a bowl. Check the vegetable shortening label for food allergies. Put about two cups in one bag. Slip a second bag inside. Tape the folded rims together and leave the inner bag open. Spread the shortening about a finger's width around the inner bag.

scenes.tts: Make a plain mitten with the other two bags and nothing between them. Squeeze out extra air so the fat is the only difference. Fill the bowl two-thirds with cold water, add two trays of ice, and wait five minutes.
scenes.caption: Make a plain mitten with the other two bags and nothing between them. Squeeze out extra air so the fat is the only difference. Fill the bowl two-thirds with cold water, add two trays of ice, and wait five minutes.
scenes.visual: The second pair of bags slides beside the blubber mitten in matching cross-section, visibly empty as gentle arrows press trapped air out. Behind them, the large bowl fills two-thirds with cool blue water, ice cubes tumble in from two trays, and a simple schematic clock hand sweeps smoothly across five minutes.
scenes.narration: Make a plain mitten with the other two bags and nothing between them. Squeeze out extra air so the fat is the only difference. Fill the bowl two-thirds with cold water, add two trays of ice, and wait five minutes.

scenes.tts: Have your child feel the shortening through the bag. Ask, 'Does it feel warm or cool?' Ask, 'Which hand will feel cold first?' Write down the guess. Have your child dip both mittens to the wrists, with the openings above water. Start the timer.
scenes.caption: Have your child feel the shortening through the bag. Ask, 'Does it feel warm or cool?' Ask, 'Which hand will feel cold first?' Write down the guess. Have your child dip both mittens to the wrists, with the openings above water. Start the timer.
scenes.visual: Schematic view: a simple illustrated hand silhouette taps the outside of the shortening mitten as a small neutral-temperature wave ripples off. Two short quote cards appear cleanly in turn, then two stylized mittened hands lower gently into the ice-water bowl up to the wrist while taped openings stay well above the waterline and the timer starts ticking.
scenes.narration: Have your child feel the shortening through the bag. Ask, 'Does it feel warm or cool?' Ask, 'Which hand will feel cold first?' Write down the guess. Have your child dip both mittens to the wrists, with the openings above water. Start the timer.

scenes.tts: Have your child say which hand feels cold as soon as they notice it. Record the time when each hand first feels cold. Stop at one minute, anytime your child wants, or at the first sign of discomfort. Dry and gently warm both hands. Wait about five minutes, until both hands feel normal. Then swap mittens and repeat.
scenes.caption: Have your child say which hand feels cold as soon as they notice it. Record the time when each hand first feels cold. Stop at one minute, anytime your child wants, or at the first sign of discomfort. Dry and gently warm both hands. Wait about five minutes, until both hands feel normal. Then swap mittens and repeat.
scenes.visual: On the carried bowl view, the plain-mitten hand shivers with a crisp 'Cold!' callout while the shortening-mitten hand stays calm and steady as the timer runs. Both mittens lift out, a warm towel wipes schematic hand silhouettes during a smooth five-minute sweep, and curved arrows swap the two mittens left-to-right for a second test.
scenes.narration: Have your child say which hand feels cold as soon as they notice it. Record the time when each hand first feels cold. Stop at one minute, anytime your child wants, or at the first sign of discomfort. Dry and gently warm both hands. Wait about five minutes, until both hands feel normal. Then swap mittens and repeat.

scenes.tts: After the test, ask your child, 'Where did that warmth come from?' Many kids say the shortening made heat, or blocked the cold from getting in. Pause for a moment and picture it yourself. Which way is heat actually moving?
scenes.caption: After the test, ask your child, 'Where did that warmth come from?' Many kids say the shortening made heat, or blocked the cold from getting in. Pause for a moment and picture it yourself. Which way is heat actually moving?
scenes.visual: Zoom cleanly into the schematic cross-section of a warm golden hand silhouette inside the pale shortening layer, surrounded by icy blue water. Bold, high-contrast question text settles at the top: 'Which way does heat move?' No directional arrows yet.
scenes.narration: After the test, ask your child, 'Where did that warmth come from?' Many kids say the shortening made heat, or blocked the cold from getting in. Pause for a moment and picture it yourself. Which way is heat actually moving?

scenes.visual: Hold the cross-section and the question 'Which way does heat move?' on screen for a calm thinking pause. Subtle shimmering ripples drift in the icy water and a soft warm pulse breathes gently around the hand outline without showing arrow direction.

scenes.tts: Heat always flows from warm places to cold ones. Cold never moves into the hand. Your child's hand made the warmth, and the fat slowed its escape. A seal has a thick layer of fat under its skin called blubber. That layer slows heat loss.
scenes.caption: Heat always flows from warm places to cold ones. Cold never moves into the hand. Your child's hand made the warmth, and the fat slowed its escape. A seal has a thick layer of fat under its skin called blubber. That layer slows heat loss.
scenes.visual: From the warm hand silhouette, golden arrows now flow outward toward the icy water—rushing fast across the plain bag side, and moving slowly through the thick pale shortening layer. The blubber cross-section morphs smoothly back into the seal cutaway from scene one, showing the same slow outward golden arrows inside the seal's blubber.
scenes.narration: Heat always flows from warm places to cold ones. Cold never moves into the hand. Your child's hand made the warmth, and the fat slowed its escape. A seal has a thick layer of fat under its skin called blubber. That layer slows heat loss.

scenes.tts: Stop for stinging, tingling, numbness, pain, or unusual skin color. Never leave a child alone with the bowl. Empty it right afterward. Keep bags and ice away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. Never use dry ice.
scenes.caption: Stop for stinging, tingling, numbness, pain, or unusual skin color. Never leave a child alone with the bowl. Empty it right afterward. Keep bags and ice away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. Never use dry ice.
scenes.visual: Carried tabletop schematic shifts to calm high-contrast safety cues, never more than four elements at once: a steady timer stopping cleanly at sixty seconds, a bowl tipping out empty, a clear 'Under 4' keep-away badge beside a zip bag and ice cube with 'Call 911 if choking', and a crossed-out dry-ice icon.
scenes.narration: Stop for stinging, tingling, numbness, pain, or unusual skin color. Never leave a child alone with the bowl. Empty it right afterward. Keep bags and ice away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. Never use dry ice.

scenes.tts: If your child skips cold water, or wants a harder test, try the guide's thermometer version. Then look at a seal together and ask where its mitten is. Ask what they noticed and how it helps explain why a seal loses heat more slowly.
